identity.title: Establishment of a RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a system-based nucleic acid detection method for avian reticuloendotheliosis virus.

content.abstract: Reticuloendotheliosis virus (REV) is an immunosuppressive and oncogenic pathogen that causes substantial economic losses in poultry production. In the absence of commercial vaccines and specific therapeutic agents against REV, early and accurate detection is essential for REV control and eradication. In this study, a visual RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay was established for REV detection based on a conserved 552-bp region of the pol gene. RAA primers and crRNA were screened, and the reaction conditions were systematically optimized. The assay was completed at 37  degrees C with 20min of RAA amplification and 40min of Cas12a reaction, and results were read visually under blue/UV light. The limit of detection was 10 copies/muL. The assay showed no cross-reactivity with other common avian pathogens and exhibited good repeatability. When 90 clinical samples were tested, the RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay detected 50 positive samples (55.55%), whereas qPCR detected 43 positive samples (47.77%). The overall agreement was 85.56% (77/90), with a positive agreement of 93.02% (40/43), a negative agreement of 78.72% (37/47), and a Cohen's kappa of 0.713. These results indicate that the RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay is a rapid, specific, and visual method for REV detection and provides a complementary tool for REV screening, although further validation with live birds and other sample types is required.
